extracted.intended_audience: researchers and doctoral students in computational linguistics / AI working on meme analysis, multimodal modeling, and knowledge-base construction
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating computational methods to analyze, classify, generate, and semantically annotate internet memes, with an emphasis on contextual sensitivity, multimodality, and knowledge-base support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextually sensitive analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational approaches should be contextually sensitive and able to embed connotative meaning or contextual information in memes, capturing referentiality and latent meaning that arise from users' continuous referencing of other meme content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper argues current computational methods 'lack the same depth and contextual sensitivity of non-computational approaches' and therefore proposes methods (meme genealogy + knowledge base) to train contextually sensitive models for analysing memes and enabling semi-automated annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal processing (image + text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches must treat memes as multimodal objects where image and text interact and provide context for one another rather than analysing text alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites the Hateful Memes Competition and SemEval Memotion work showing the interplay of text and image can change classification; recommends extracting features from visual streams and jointly modelling visual and textual signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of external knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Models should exploit external knowledge sources to augment understanding of memes, using contextual information gathered from meme-specific online sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed knowledge base will 'match [features inherent in memes] with contextual knowledge from online sources' drawing on successful prior models that leverage external knowledge to improve performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meme genealogy and taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a 'meme genealogy' and taxonomy that identifies prominent features and relationships between memes to map meme families and feature-inheritance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The genealogy is intended to inform a knowledge base and allow mapping of relationships via identified features; leveraging family/entity relationships enables minimal annotation and analysis of emerging memes by shared features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meme-specific ontology / knowledge base
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a meme-specific ontology and knowledge base to collate contextual information, ensuring the connotations and references that memes encode are captured and represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The knowledge base should be constructed from meme-specific online sources, embedding connotative meanings and references as memes are continually produced and recontextualized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semi-automated annotation with minimal supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems should be able to tag memes with relevant semantic and contextual knowledge while requiring minimal manual annotation (only a few templates or features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploiting 'meme families' and feature-inheritance allows minimal annotation of a few meme templates or features to support future analysis and to apply annotations to new, emerging memes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-grained sentiment and discourse analysis (multimodal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for fine-grained emotion and discourse classification applied to both visual and textual components of memes rather than unimodal approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SemEval 2020 Task 8 (Memotion) shows multimodal methods outperform unimodal ones but overall performance remains poor, indicating room for improvement and the need for richer contextual representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiotic analysis of visual/textual codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a semiotic framework to analyse the visual and textual codes in memes to understand how meaning is constructed across modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The semiotic framework is expected to be applied after the knowledge base construction to help disentangle intra-modal dynamics and referentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature extraction using computer vision and NLP
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract prominent meme features via computer vision and natural language processing to support classification and the construction of the genealogy/taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature extraction forms the basis for mapping relationships between memes; the planned first pass has focused on extracting features for the knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness and generalizability to 'memes in the wild'
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and models should generalize beyond artificial or competition datasets to perform well on 'wild' meme data encountered in real-world social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kirk et al. (2021) observed models from the Hateful Memes competition performed poorly on wild meme classification, highlighting the need to avoid overfitting to artificial datasets and to improve generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template-aware text-image alignment for generation
rubrics_metrics.description: In meme generation tasks, text must be correctly aligned to the appropriate meme template and the model must understand template-specific linguistic/visual codes to avoid confusing structures across templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior AI meme generation work used text-image alignment but demonstrated limited understanding by confusing common linguistic structures of one meme template with another; improved template awareness is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset representativeness and labeling granularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use or create datasets that are multimodal, representative of real-world meme usage, and provide sufficiently fine-grained emotion/labeling to support nuanced analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memotion (a prelabelled dataset with fine-grained emotions) was useful but models still performed poorly; datasets should be designed to reflect true meme variation and contextual dependencies.
